title: My Kinsta Review | Good managed WordPress hosting?
text: My Kinsta Review tl;dr: I’ve been in WordPress for 15 years. Ran an agency for 10 years. Producing a WordPress podcast for 11 years. Worked at a WordPress hosting company for 3 years. Kinsta has been the best experience for me and I highly recommend it if you can afford it. Note: These are affiliate links. If you use them, I make a little cash. It helps pay for producing this podcast and hosting at Kinsta. Get started at Kinsta Listen to this review instead : Click play if you prefer to listen to this Kinsta review Pricing Kinsta’s pricing is a touch on the higher side of your typical Managed WordPress host. A few month’s prior to this post, they increased my monthly bill by +$10 USD. I didn’t care. The speed, support, and overall user experience has been fantastic. Some of that stuff I’ll cover in a moment. If you can afford the “higher end” of hosting, $35/mo for 1 website (or $70 for two, which is what I pay) but pays for itself in overall value. Visit Kinsta now Support Previous to moving my site to Kinsta, I was self-hosting at Digital Ocean. I used a control panel that helped me manage sites and other basic functionality, but all troubleshooting and uptime concerns were mine to lose sleep over. And believe me, I did. Kinsta provides a white-glove service to migrate your existing site over, which was the first interaction I had with their support. Well, besides the fact that I use to sell against them at a WordPress hosting company I worked at years ago… They were fantastic! The moved everything over in timely fashion and communicated with me the whole time. Migrating my WordPress website to Kinsta was a breeze. Support response times I didn’t make a spreadsheet of tracked timestamps, but the 6 -10 times I’ve had a support question, they answered it in minutes. No helpdesk ticket, no stupid robot “choose your own adventure” chat bot — a human on the other end. Helping. Me. I trust Kinsta support! I think most top-tier managed WordPress hosting companies are just competing in the margins for features. Speed, backups, staging…we all expect that in 2022 from a decent host. Support, on the other hand, is not created equal. Kinsta is leading the pack imo. Visit Kinsta now Speed Uhh…fast. Really fast. And I’m not talking just the front-end page speed tests. The admin was faster, when I was pulling up the post editor to write, everything felt snappier. But…that’s what I expected. I didn’t expect my DIY setup to lightning quick. Sure, I was a server admin 20 years ago, but that was twenty years ago! I expected that, if I were going to pay 3x what it cost me to host on my own servers, that speed was going to be part of the deal. And best of all, it wasn’t me that had to worry about it. Kinsta is quick Let me pull back on all this sugar coating for a second. There are a lot of great hosting companies that get flack for poor speed results from their customers. Heck, I’m sure Kinsta gets their fair share. What WordPress hosting customers need to realize is this: Invest in a solid hosting company Invest in a well-coded WordPress theme Understand the plugins you’re using If you found this review because your web host is slow, Kinsta might not be the answer you’re hoping for. Did you get a solid theme? Are you using too many plugins? Optimize your WordPress stack before making the swtich. Visit Kinsta now Control Panel Features If there’s no button for it, does it even exist? Me, I said that At my old WordPress hosting gig, we lacked a lot of features. Features that, back then, we’d lose deals to Kinsta to because the customer couldn’t find them. Some of them existed, but they were too technical. There was not — say it with me — a magical button. Kinsta has the buttons, and they have a lot of them. This isn’t a technical review, just an honest dialogue about my experiences using Kinsta. My favorite features that I use regularly are: Staging/backup process at Kinsta is the cleanest I’ve experienced DNS records and management are a breeze Graphs and reporting keep me in-the-know about traffic and my monthly bill Activity log will show me any configuration or account changes that my login, my team’s login, or even Kinsta’s support have made. Kinsta’s control panel gives you everything you need to manage your WordPress installs, clone/deploy staging environments, and dial in your infrastructure. It doesn’t have everything and the kitchen sink like cPanel…but that’s the point. Visit Kinsta now That’s it for my Kinsta review. If you think Kinsta is right for you, please consider clicking the button above to sign up. If the WordPress community, ecosystem, or economy is important to you — please tune in to my podcast.

title: Kinsta Review: PHP limits, add-ons, and Cloudflare are poor
headings: 4. Low Visit, Bandwidth, WP Install, Storage Limits
6. Amazon Route 53’s DNS Is Slower Than Cloudflare
text: Kinsta started as a marketing company and is backed by M-One Capital (that should tell you something). Their add-ons include charging you for open source software (like $100/month for Redis or $50/month for Nginx reverse proxy) while other add-ons expose their stingy resource limits . PHP threads and memory limits are one of their most common complaints , so you’ll need their PHP Performance add-on to fix that. Want more than 10GB storage on your $142/month hosting plan? You’ll need their disk space add-on. And unless you pay $20/month for premium staging environments, staging sites get 1 CPU core . More than 1 WordPress install ? Add-on. Plus, resources aren’t dedicated (otherwise they wouldn’t make you drop $300+/month for the dedicated resources add-on) while bandwidth and monthly visits are similar to WP Engine’s. Kinsta starves you of resources then sells them to you as add-ons (along with open source software) Kinsta’s Cloudflare integration has been described as “ the f*cking worst ” and isn’t Cloudflare Enterprise. Also not sure why you would use Amazon Route 53’s DNS when Cloudflare is faster . IMO, this is a classic example of “managed WordPress hosting” that overcharges people who have no clue what kind of resources, performance, or value they’re getting. Don’t be that guy. 100% agree. Avoid Kinsta’s arbitrary limits and pay for the CPU cores, RAM, and storage your site needs ( source ) Beware of PHP limits 1 CPU core on staging sites $100/mo Redis + $50/mo Nginx reverse proxy Low visit, bandwidth, WP install, storage limits Poor Cloudflare integration (and not Enterprise) Amazon Route 53’s DNS is slower than Cloudflare Why the price increase?! Google Cloud C2 → C3D MU plugin No email hosting Banned plugins OK support, not the best Kinsta alternatives 1. Beware Of PHP Limits Read the complaints because this is how they get you to upgrade. PHP workers determine how many uncached requests your site can handle at once while the PHP memory limit is stuck at 256MB unless you’re dropping $625/month for Single 1.25M visits. So if you have a dynamic site (e.g. WooCommerce), you’re probably looking at $300+/mo between a plan with more workers and $100/Redis which is specifically good for dynamic sites. $1500/month and they can’t handle 100 concurrent checkouts?! As one reviewer says , you are paying an extortionate rate to sabotage your WooCommerce website 2. 1 CPU Core On Staging Sites To jump from 1 CPU core to 12 cores, you’ll pay $20/month for premium staging environments . 3. $100/mo Redis + $50/mo Nginx Reverse Proxy Funny thing is, Kinsta recommends using Redis to optimize PHP workers . So if you run out of PHP workers (which is common), their solution is to drop $100/month on open source software. 4. Low Visit, Bandwidth, WP Install, Storage Limits Visits counts are different from Google Analytics which count human visitors not using ad blockers. Kinsta counts human visitors (with or without ad blockers) as well as unknown bots. To calculate visit counts, multiply your Google Analytics monthly visits by 1.685 (since ~31.5% of people use ad blockers and ~37% of traffic is unknown bots ). If you take the time to block bad bots in Cloudflare’s firewall and Kinsta’s IP/user-agent banning rules, you can lower it. Server bandwidth starts at just 20GB, storage starts at 10GB, and you only get 1 WordPress install across plans (unless you purchase their disk space add-on or upgrade to agency plans ). 5. Poor Cloudflare Integration (And Not Enterprise) Kinsta’s Cloudflare integration doesn’t support several Cloudflare features . One is Argo Smart Routing which normally shaves an average 33% off TTFB and is great for speeding up dynamic pages like cart, checkout, and account pages. No Argo Smart Routing, no Redis, skimping on resources… this is why I don’t consider Kinsta optimized for eCommerce . Plus, Kinsta previously claimed they were using an “enterprise-level Cloudflare integration” when in fact, it lacked way too many features to be considered Cloudflare Enterprise. That’s probably why people said it was “ terrible and misleading ” and that it was a “ nerfed Cloudflare .” You’re better off using FlyingCDN’s Cloudflare Enterprise or Cloudflare directly (with APO and possibly other paid features like Argo) so you’re not tied to a host because of their Cloudflare integration. I recently switched from Rocket.net (who I was using because of their Cloudflare Enterprise) but switched to FlyingCDN, then a host with faster hardware than CPUs from 2013 . 6. Amazon Route 53’s DNS Is Slower Than Cloudflare Kinsta uses Amazon Route 53 for their DNS, but Cloudflare performs better on dnsperf.com . 7. Why The Price Increase?! If Kinsta wasn’t expensive already, they previously raised their prices which some customers reported a 42% price increase based on Kinsta’s new limits on visitors, installs, and disk usage. Kinsta’s old prices 8. Google Cloud C2 → C3D Kinsta’s boosted regions use Google Cloud C3D which to their credit, use faster AMD EPYC 9004 series processors than C2 machines (what Kinsta previously used on non-boosted regions). It’s also why Kinsta is faster than WP Engine who still use C2 and SiteGround who use the N2 series . 9. MU Plugin Kinsta’s MU plugin is required for their CDN and full page caching. This enables automatic cache clearing, custom caching rules, and changing the cache expiry in MyKinsta (default is 1 hour). It’s installed on every website hosted at Kinsta by default, but will need to be manually installed if you migrated your website yourself or you installed WordPress. Kinsta says no WordPress cache plugins are needed at Kinsta and even bans some of them. However, cache plugins do a lot more than just caching and are a key part of addressing core web vitals. Which means you’ll still want a cache plugin (i.e. FlyingPress). Kinsta automatically disables caching in WP Rocket, but you’ll have to check whether they also do it for FlyingPress. 10. No Email Hosting Kinsta doesn’t have email hosting and recommends Google Workspace instead. It’s a good idea to keep your web/email hosting separate anyways because resources can be solely dedicated to your website (plus, moving email accounts between hosts can be a pain). 11. Banned Plugins Kinsta has a list of banned plugins . Hosts often do this because these plugins are notorious for increasing memory usage or cause duplicate functionality. For example, since Kinsta already provides Enterprise-level security through Cloudflare, you shouldn’t need any security plugin. Cache plugins Backup plugins Image optimization plugins Video conversion plugins Certain performance plugins Security plugins 12. OK Support, Not The Best Kinsta’s support used to be good, but how good can it be when you constantly run out of resources? With all their limits, I imagine you get the “ upgrade your plan ” response quite a bit. 13. Kinsta Alternatives I’m going to leave this here again: I switched from Rocket.net (who I previously recommended as my main Kinsta alternative) to ScalaHosting’s VPS because their hardware is a lot faster. Their AMD EPYC 9474F CPUs are top 2.5% fastest server CPUs ( ~31/1178 ) and built for concurrency since their multithread rating is 480% higher than Rocket’s Intel Xeon E5-2667 v2 CPUs with DDR5 RAM and PCIe 5.0 NVMe SSDs . ScalaHosting’s AMD EPYC 9474F CPUs are ~31st/1178 fastest on PassMark Rocket.net Rocket.net (PHP Vitals) ScalaHosting VPS (Build #1) ScalaHosting (PHP Vitals) Then I used FlyingCDN for Cloudflare Enterprise which gave me a 50ms global TTFB , and in the end, Hosting Benchmark Tool scores were faster (along with a ~2x faster frontend + wp-admin). ~50ms global TTFB is easy when FlyingCDN’s Cloudflare Enterprise lets you prioritize hosting hardware https://onlinemediamasters.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/ScalaHosting-wp-admin-speed.mp4 While they’re more similar to Cloudways (a VPS without limits ), they use a more lightweight SPanel which supports OpenLiteSpeed , full root access, and a lot more features Cloudways doesn’t support (plus they’re independently owned and cost significantly less for 1 to 3 years). Build your own VPS so you know exactly how many resources you’re getting If you want “managed hosting,” find an experienced freelancer (sysadmin) to set up third-party tools to monitor and manage your site. This will likely cost less and you’re not shoveling money to hosts who are only “managing” to extort you and your money. Kinsta Alternatives I Don’t Recommend Rocket.net : too many empty promises on their “fastest hosting” (they use CPUs from 2013), “independence” (now acquired by hosting.com), and “high converting product” (they reverse up to 76% of affiliate sales). I no longer trust what they say, plus, they have several arbitrary limits like Kinsta (bandwidth being the main one). Cloudways : fails in performance, support, and value (price vs resources) since they add 220% markups compared to what’s listed on DigitalOcean or Vultr with many unwanted changes after DigitalOcean’s acquisition. Cloudflare Enterprise integration is poor and same with Object Cache Pro which doesn’t support Relay (a key performance feature). Spams Reddit + Facebook groups with fake reviews. WP Engine : very similar to Kinsta with arbitrary limits, backed by private equity, and uses Google Cloud C2 which is slower than C3D boosted regions with Kinsta. SiteGround : they got so greedy in 2019 and have gone terribly downhill (and hit you with disk I/O limits on their cloud hosting which cause 503 errors + upgrades). Looks like Kinsta fixed their TrustPilot rating which is now 4.9/5, but don’t let that fool you. Cheers, Tom Related:

Kinsta also handles free migrations for existing WordPress sites. Modern dashboard The Kinsta dashboard looks great and loads quickly. And usually, you'll know right away during setup, whether a provider delivers on that promise. Kinsta nails ease of use from the start. Creating an account is quick, and you won't have to wait for your hosting plan to activate. You can jump right into the Kinsta dashboard. The dashboard greets you with a key choice: migrate an existing website to Kinsta or create a new one. Either way, a setup assistant walks you through the process. Installing WordPress on Kinsta is fast and simple. Installing WordPress on Kinsta: fast and simple Unlike some other managed hosts, Kinsta doesn't pre-install WordPress. But that's no problem, since setting up a new WordPress site is quick. To get started, select "Create Site" in the Kinsta dashboard and choose a new WordPress installation. WordPress installs in just a few clicks. Next, choose an internal name for your site and select a data center location. Kinsta offers plenty of options worldwide. Pick your website name and server location. Next, set up your WordPress admin login. If you'd like, Kinsta can also install add-ons like WooCommerce, Yoast SEO, or Easy Digital Downloads for you. Just a few minutes later, you can log in to your WordPress dashboard and start building your site. In our test, the installation was ready in about three minutes. The only pre-installed plugins were two default WordPress plugins and Kinsta’s caching plugin. WordPress installs quickly and easily. Easy WordPress migration handled by the Kinsta team If you already have a WordPress site with another host, you can request a migration through the Kinsta dashboard, and Kinsta’s team will handle the move for you. Unlike some other hosts, Kinsta doesn’t officially offer a semi-automated, plugin-based migration . For a standard migration, you’ll rely on Kinsta’s support team unless you want to handle it yourself. Don’t expect the move to be done in half an hour. You can choose when the migration happens. By default, Kinsta starts as soon as possible and usually finishes within one business day, Monday through Friday. You may also choose a preferred time or even pay extra for an express migration, which Kinsta guarantees will be completed within eight hours. In our test, we opted for a migration "as soon as possible." You choose when the migration happens. No matter which option you pick, Kinsta walks you through the migration request step by step: 1. Choose your migration source Decide whether Kinsta should pull your site from another host or restore it from a backup. For a standard move, pick the first option. 2. Name your current host Next, select your current provider. The list of supported hosts leans heavily toward US companies and includes Bluehost , Cloudways , DreamHost , GoDaddy , SiteGround, and WP Engine . If your host isn't listed, choose “Other.” 3. Provide access to your old host Kinsta needs access to your existing hosting account so the team can export your site's data. Depending on your provider, you'll enter the login URL, username, and password. FTP credentials may also be required. 4. Enter your WordPress credentials Enter the domain of your old site along with the login details for your WordPress dashboard. If you run a multisite, a WooCommerce store , or a large membership site, flag that here too. It helps the Kinsta team plan the move. 5. Set up your new Kinsta site Give your site an internal name and choose a data center location. If most of your visitors are in the US, pick a data center close to them. You can also use the notes field to flag special plugins or other quirks the team should know about. 6. Submit your request Kinsta shows you a summary of everything you entered. Double-check it carefully, since the migration team works directly from this information. When you're satisfied, submit the request. During our test, Kinsta's team completed the migration the same day without asking a single follow-up question. After about four hours , the site had been migrated and appeared in the dashboard as an unpublished preview. In other words, Kinsta's free migration was faster than our previous host's paid expedited service. Once your site was migrated successfully, or if you've simply installed a fresh WordPress instance, you can start working in the Kinsta dashboard. A modern Kinsta dashboard Kinsta's interface shows just how pleasant hosting management can be these days. Even first-time users should find their way around quickly, since every key feature is right where you’d expect it to be. Performance is excellent too: pages load almost instantly, and even larger sections stay smooth and responsive. The Kinsta dashboard is one of the fastest we've tested. The design feels modern and restrained. Generous spacing, clean typography, and clearly labeled buttons make it easy to find your way around. Kinsta uses color sparingly, drawing your eye to the elements that matter most. The Kinsta dashboard is clean and modern. The home screen gives you a full overview of your site's status. Visitor numbers, available updates, the PHP version in use, and any detected security issues are all visible at a glance. Below that, Kinsta shows recent activity and lists your latest notifications. Detailed statistics are another dashboard strength. Kinsta clearly displays visitor numbers, bandwidth usage, CDN traffic, and storage consumption. The built-in analytics provide all the key metrics. Easy setup, thoughtful design Kinsta shows what getting started with managed WordPress hosting should look like today. The platform automates tasks where it makes sense, but still gives you enough freedom without oversimplifying important features. Very few providers manage to strike that balance. We see room for improvement in only one area: adding an option to migrate WordPress sites yourself. It would make an already strong first impression even better. Even without that feature, Kinsta stands out as one of the best providers we tested when it comes to setup and ease of use. 2. PHP version configurable Max PHP version 8.5 512 MB memory_limit 300s max_execution_time 128 MB upload_max_filesize 5.5/8 Caching & CDN ? Server side caching CDN Cache exclusions Automatic cache purge 4/5 Features ? Cron jobs, SSH, WP-CLI WordPress Multisite in almost all plans Staging available 5/5 The technology behind a managed WordPress host determines how flexible, fast, and future-proof it really is. Many features work quietly in the background, but they can still have a noticeable impact on load times and how much upkeep you need to do. Let’s take a closer look at what Kinsta offers on the technical side. Modern hosting infrastructure with a few small drawbacks For its web server , Kinsta relies on NGINX. This modern server software handles many simultaneous requests smoothly and powers many high-performance hosting platforms today. It’s a solid choice for managed WordPress hosting. With 27 data centers across 21 countries, Kinsta offers more location options than any other provider we tested. You can choose your website’s location yourself and place it as close as possible to your target audience. Shorter distances between the server and your visitors typically mean faster load times. Kinsta Bluehost Cloudways DreamHost GoDaddy Hostinger IONOS SiteGround WordPress.com WP Engine Server locations 21 countries 9 countries 8 countries 3 countries 3 countries 11 countries 2 countries 7 countries 19 countries 12 countries Web server NGINX Apache NGINX NGINX NGINX LiteSpeed Apache NGINX NGINX NGINX Control Panel Custom cPanel Custom Custom Custom Custom Custom Custom Custom Custom Database MariaDB MySQL MariaDB MySQL MySQL MariaDB MariaDB MySQL MariaDB MySQL Storage type HDD NVMe HDD HDD HDD HDD HDD HDD SSD HDD Protocols HTTP/2 ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ HTTP/3 ✓ ✗ ✗ ✗ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✗ ✓ ✓ Kinsta uses traditional SSD storage rather than NVMe SSDs. NVMe drives offer faster transfer speeds and are now standard with many hosting providers, so Kinsta falls behind on storage technology. For its database system , Kinsta uses MariaDB, a modern successor to MySQL that's fully compatible with WordPress. Kinsta keeps up with the latest network protocols . HTTP/2 speeds up loading by transferring multiple files at once. HTTP/3 goes even further, improving speed and stability, especially on slow or unstable connections. Kinsta supports both, which is great news for customers. PHP up to version 8.5 Running the latest PHP version is relevant for both performance and security. At the time of this review, Kinsta supports PHP versions 7.4 through 8.5, which is the latest available release. Multiple PHP versions to choose from. You can’t adjust the memory limit, max execution time, or upload size directly in Kinsta’s dashboard. This isn’t unusual for managed WordPress hosting, since many providers set fixed values for all customers. The available memory determines how many resources WordPress can use for tasks. If it’s too low, larger backups or plugin updates may fail. Our reference plan includes 512 MB, though some plans offer only 256 MB. The max execution time is a generous 300 seconds, which sets how long WordPress can run a task before the server stops it. The 128 MB upload limit works for most WordPress projects, though it’s not the highest we’ve seen. Kinsta Bluehost Cloudways DreamHost GoDaddy Hostinger IONOS SiteGround WordPress.com WP Engine PHP version configurable ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ PHP settings configurable ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✗ Max PHP version 8.5 8.5 8.4 8.5 8.3 8.5 8.4 8.5 8.4 8.4 Max memory limit 512 MB unlimited unlimited 768 MB 512 MB 3072 MB 512 MB 768 MB 512 MB 512 MB Max execution time 300s unlimited unlimited unlimited 180s unlimited 360s 120s 850s 43300s Max upload size 128 MB unlimited unlimited 1028 MB 1024 MB 3072 MB 128 MB 256 MB 2048 MB 50 MB Kinsta takes a different approach to PHP memory. Instead of assigning a fixed amount of RAM to each PHP instance, the host uses a shared memory pool. You decide whether to allocate the available memory to more PHP threads or to give each thread more RAM. Kinsta’s shared memory pool. If you need more memory, you can expand the pool for an extra fee. That gives you far more flexibility than a fixed memory limit. Fast performance with edge caching Caching is one of the most important features of a managed WordPress host. It stores frequently accessed content so the server doesn’t have to generate it from scratch on every visit. This speeds up load times, reduces server strain, and improves overall performance. The more modern caching techniques a host uses, the better. Kinsta covers almost all the bases. The only thing missing is Object Cache, which isn’t included in the standard plan. Kinsta Bluehost Cloudways DreamHost GoDaddy Hostinger IONOS SiteGround WordPress.com WP Engine Server side caching ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Object Caching ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ CDN ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✓ ✓ Cache exclusions ✓ ✓ ✓ ✗ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✓ ✗ ✓ Automatic cache purge ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Server-side caching stores fully generated WordPress pages directly on the server. Visitors get the content instantly, without WordPress or the database having to work on every page load. Kinsta enables this by default for all websites. Edge caching takes it a step further. Kinsta doesn’t cache individual files, it stores entire pages on Cloudflare’s global network. Visitors get the full webpage from the closest server location. Edge caching distributes full webpages across Cloudflare’s network. A content delivery network (CDN) distributes images, CSS, JavaScript, and other static files across servers worldwide. Visitors automatically load these files from the nearest location, which speeds up load times and eases the load on your main web server. Kinsta includes a CDN at no extra cost. Manage the CDN through the Kinsta dashboard. Object Cache stores frequently used database queries in memory. This is especially useful for WooCommerce stores and other database-heavy websites. Kinsta offers this feature only as a paid Redis add-on. Redis is available as a paid add-on at Kinsta. Kinsta adds a dedicated cache management menu in the WordPress backend. There, you can clear the entire cache or only the Page Cache, Object Cache, or CDN Cache. This saves time when you're already working in your WordPress admin. Cache management in the WordPress backend. To see if these performance features actually make a difference, check out the Performance section . Other Kinsta features Kinsta offers many more features than we can cover in detail here. These are the most important ones: Staging environments Create a staging environment for each WordPress install. It’s completely separate from your live site, so you can test new features and changes before going live. DevKinsta Use DevKinsta to develop and test WordPress sites locally on your computer, then transfer them seamlessly to Kinsta’s platform. Cloning Clone your websites and staging environments with one click. This is great for creating templates for future projects. Analytics Kinsta’s built-in analytics let you track metrics like visitor numbers, PHP speeds, server resource usage, and where your visitors come from. SFTP, SSH, WP-CLI, Cronjobs Kinsta supports SFTP and SSH access for file management. It also includes WP-CLI, so you can handle many WordPress tasks from the command line. You can set up cron jobs, too. Multisites Kinsta supports WordPress multisites in almost all managed plans. You can run multiple websites within a single WordPress installation. Geolocation Kinsta can detect the approximate location of your visitors, which lets you set up different redirects by country or region. For example, you can automatically direct visitors to the appropriate language version of your site. Banned WordPress Plugins Not every WordPress plugin works with Kinsta. The host blocks or restricts some of them outright. This usually applies to plugins that duplicate features Kinsta already provides or could hurt server performance or stability. For the full list, check Kinsta’s knowledge base . Here’s what’s blocked: Caching and performance plugins like Cache Enabler, Better WordPress Minify, P3 Profiler, or JCH Optimize. Kinsta says its built-in caching and optimization tools make these plugins unnecessary. Backup and migration tools such as All-in-One WP Migration, BackupBuddy, Updraft, or Duplicator Pro. Kinsta handles backups automatically and recommends using its own tools for site migrations. Server-based image optimizers and video converters using FFmpeg. Kinsta says these can put too much strain on its servers. Many security plugins either don’t work at all or offer limited functionality. Wordfence, for example, still works, but it won’t log traffic on Kinsta’s servers. No free domains or email hosting It’s disappointing that Kinsta doesn’t include free domains or email hosting, not even in its most expensive plans. Most other WordPress hosts offer these as standard. That stings all the more since Kinsta already costs more than many competitors. Solid features with a few gaps Kinsta’s tech stack is strong enough to handle just about any WordPress project. The host uses modern infrastructure where it counts and covers most needs well. But it’s not perfect. NVMe storage is standard with many competitors, while Object Cache costs extra. Still, these gaps don’t change the big picture: Kinsta is one of the most powerful managed WordPress hosts we’ve tested. 3. Security Security (10%) 5.6 / 10 Free SSL ? No 0/2 Server protection ? Firewall DDoS protection Login protection Malware scanning 4/4 WordPress updates ? No automatic updates 0/2 Backups ? Daily backups aren't included in every plan 0/2 A managed WordPress host’s most important job is keeping your site safe. What matters isn’t just the security features it offers, but how much of the work it handles for you automatically. SSL certificates come standard with Kinsta, as you’d expect from a managed WordPress host, even if you connect an existing domain. You don’t have to lift a finger. Kinsta automatically requests the certificate through Cloudflare, sets it up, and renews it, so your website stays encrypted at all times. Protection against malware and attacks A firewall protects your website in every plan. It checks incoming requests and blocks suspicious traffic before it reaches your web server. Kinsta uses Cloudflare for this. The new bot protection goes a step further. You choose from multiple security levels and decide how strictly Kinsta should treat suspicious bots or unknown visitors. Depending on your settings, Kinsta blocks only clearly harmful traffic or also verifies suspicious requests. Adjust the bot protection to your desired security level. Some attackers try to overload a website with a flood of simultaneous requests until it crashes. Kinsta automatically detects these DDoS attacks and filters out the harmful traffic before it reaches your site. From the dashboard, you can also set up your own security rules. For example, you can block individual IP addresses to keep out unwanted visitors. You can block IP addresses through the Kinsta dashboard. Other attacks target the WordPress login. Automated programs try countless username and password combinations in a short time to break into your site. Kinsta automatically detects these brute-force attacks . After several failed login attempts, it temporarily blocks the offending IP address. Kinsta also automatically detects malware. If a website gets hacked despite all security measures, Kinsta removes the malware for free. Not all hosts do this. Kinsta detects and removes malware for you. Backups kept for at least 14 days Kinsta creates a backup of your WordPress site every day and before major changes, so you can restore an older version if something goes wrong. In the standard plans, Kinsta keeps these automatic backups for 14 days, which is shorter than most competitors. Only the more expensive plans offer longer retention. You can also create up to five manual backups. Kinsta stores these for 14 days by default as well. Kinsta backs up your website every day. Need more frequent backups? You can schedule automatic backups every six hours or even hourly. For an extra fee, you can also store backups externally on AWS or Google Cloud. Hourly backups are available for an extra fee. 3 ways to handle WordPress updates You can fix many security gaps in plugins or themes simply by installing updates on time. That’s why it’s surprising that Kinsta disables automatic updates by default. Before you can change this setting, you'll need to choose an update strategy. We haven't seen this option at any other managed WordPress host we've tested. Usually, at least the auto-updates managed by WordPress are turned on by default. You have to choose one of three update strategies. If you turn on the standard "WordPress auto-updates," WordPress checks for new plugin and theme versions twice a day and installs them automatically. However, it won't detect problems caused by an update. You'll need to verify for yourself that your site still works properly afterward. Kinsta's paid update service offers more protection. Before every update, the host creates an automatic backup, then compares screenshots of your site from before and after. If it spots major differences, it automatically restores the backup. The Kinsta dashboard also gives you a clear overview of all your plugins and themes. You can see which updates are available and which versions are installed, all without logging in to the WordPress backend. You manage updates directly from the Kinsta dashboard. One more thing worth noting about WordPress core updates: Kinsta doesn't handle them itself. Instead, it leaves the job to WordPress's built-in update feature. Kinsta's paid service only covers plugins and themes. Performance Performance (30%) 8.8 / 10 Response speed (TTFB) ? 0.23 s 10/10 TTFB outliers ? 0.09 % 5/5 Pagespeed (LCP) ? 0.68 s 6/10 Uptime ? 99.98 % 2/5 For our performance test, we tested Kinsta under the same conditions as every other managed WordPress host in our comparison. We picked a plan in the $20-per-month price range and installed an identical WordPress website using the page builder Elementor. We then monitored it over six weeks. Along with load times, we also checked server availability, stability under continuous use, and the impact of built-in caching on performance. You can find the full breakdown of our testing method in our article on the fastest WordPress hosts . Specifically, we measure four key metrics: 1. Response speed (TTFB): How quickly does the server respond to the first request for a page? 2. Slow responses (outliers): How much does server speed vary during unusually slow requests? 3. Pagespeed (largest contentful paint): How fast does the most important visible content on the website appear? 4. Availability (uptime): How reliably does the website stay online without downtime? TTFB test: very fast server responses Time to First Byte (TTFB) measures how long a server takes to send its first response to the browser after a website is requested. With a TTFB of 0.232 seconds , Kinsta lands in 3rd place out of 14 providers in our comparison: Response time (TTFB) WP Engine 0.186 s Bluehost 0.23 s Kinsta 0.232 s SiteGround 0.264 s Cloudways 0.266 s GoDaddy 0.271 s Hostinger 0.305 s IONOS 0.387 s WordPress.com 0.631 s DreamHost 0.819 s That result puts Kinsta among the top performers. The servers respond quickly, laying a solid foundation for short load times. Visitors to a Kinsta-hosted site won't have to deal with long, potentially costly wait times. Almost no outliers We flagged any request as a TTFB outlier if the server took longer than one second to respond. This happened only nine times out of 10,000 requests. Very fast High quality 3/3 Ratings on review platforms ? Pros 3/3 Managed WordPress hosting should take as much work off your hands as possible, especially when problems arise. A provider’s true test is how well it handles them. A good knowledge base lets you solve minor issues on your own. When that’s not enough, you should be able to reach a knowledgeable support agent without hassle. Kinsta’s support setup is solid. It includes Kinsta Docs (a knowledge base), an AI chat, live chat with support staff, and a community forum. What’s missing is a traditional ticket system or email support. If the live chat can’t resolve your issue, the support team creates an internal ticket, but you can’t open or track it yourself. Phone support isn’t available either. Strong knowledge base Kinsta Docs is the provider’s extensive knowledge base. It focuses on hosting itself, with plenty of guides for setting up, managing, and troubleshooting your hosting environment. The articles are well organized, often include helpful screenshots, and explain each step clearly. The translated version is well done too. We didn’t notice any significant language errors. Kinsta’s robust knowledge base, Kinsta Docs. Despite its focus on hosting, Kinsta doesn’t skimp on general WordPress topics. The documentation includes a somewhat hidden section called “Learn WordPress,” with guides on themes, plugins, security, and administration. This makes the knowledge base useful not just for solving specific problems, but also for learning WordPress from the ground up. Solid AI and live chat support Kinsta Docs also includes an AI chatbot. It knows the documentation inside out and reliably answers questions about plans or specific features. In our tests, it almost always gave the right answer right away, saving time and often making it unnecessary to dig through the documentation. The downside? The AI chat doesn’t hand off to a human agent when it can’t solve your problem. Instead, you have to open the separate live chat and explain your issue all over again. Frustrating: the AI chat can’t transfer conversations to live support. For direct support, you’ll mostly rely on live chat, which works well in practice. Our questions were answered quickly, and the agents addressed our specific issues instead of just pointing us to help articles. Customers can ask questions in their preferred language. Kinsta automatically translates the responses. Get help from the Kinsta community forum Kinsta also runs its own community forum, where Kinsta staff and other users answer questions. This adds real-world experience to the mix, since users share practical solutions from their day-to-day work. You can also get help in the community forum. For urgent issues, though, the forum isn’t the best option. Responses can take time, and the quality depends on who answers. No (real) email support, no phone line Kinsta doesn’t offer traditional email support. Every request starts in the live chat. If the team can’t resolve your issue there, they create a ticket in the background, but you won’t have access to it yourself. There’s also no phone support. If you prefer talking to someone directly or need immediate help with a critical issue, Kinsta doesn’t offer that option. What do customers say about Kinsta’s support? On review sites, customers praise the fast help in live chat and the expertise of the support team. They also appreciate that agents tackle the actual problem instead of just sending generic help articles. Some customers criticize the lack of phone support and the fact that not every issue can be resolved right away in live chat. A few report that more complex problems get passed to other team members, which can slow things down. Others are frustrated when support refers them to the documentation instead. Fast help, but mostly via chat The fast and knowledgeable live chat support is impressive. Our requests were translated automatically, but communication still went smoothly. Kinsta also offers extensive help resources and a forum with a fairly active community. More support options would be welcome, though, as Kinsta isn’t available by phone or email. 6. The plans fall into two main categories: single-site and multi-site WordPress hosting. The differences further come down to server bandwidth, storage space, and how long backups are kept. text: Kinsta Black Friday Offer Offer: Get 3 Months Off Discount · Last checked: November 9, 2026 Affiliate link — WebHostingCat may earn a commission if you purchase (at no extra cost for you). In our recent study of the Fastest WordPress Hosting, Kinsta ranked number overall. Kinsta’s page loading speed, Core Web Vitals and load testing results were the best of any managed WordPress host we tested. Take a look at some of our results: Speed Testing via GTmetrix Performance: 100% Structure: 100% Fully Loaded Time: 444ms First Contentful Paint (FCP): 342ms Speed Index: 344ms Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): 342ms Time to Interactive: 342ms Total Blocking Time: 0ms Cumulative Layout Shift : 0 Time to First Byte: 77ms Load Testing via loader.io Response Times: 32ms Avg. 228ms Max Reliability: 100% Success Rate No Timeouts Throughput: 100MB Delivered 1000 Requests Handled No Network Bottlenecks Best Managed WordPress Hosting Is Kinsta really that good? Is Kinsta hosting worth the price? If you’re looking for premium managed WordPress hosting, you’ll want to read my Kinsta Review here. Over the years, we’ve reviewed quite a few managed WordPress hosting options. And, from my personal experience I can tell a great WordPress host from the wannabes. Here’s how Kinsta performs and stacks up with the competition. > Try Kinsta for Free Kinsta Background Founded in 2013, Kinsta’s goal was and continues to be to provide the best WordPress hosting platform in the world—particularly for those website owners dissatisfied with the status quo WordPress hosting offerings. Kinsta Hosting Plans Kinsta has separate hosting plan packages for single sites, multiple sites, and agencies. They also have custom enterprise hosting plans available. Single Site Plans start at $30 mo., while Multiple Site Plans start at $59 mo. Agency hosting starts at $284 mo. Click Here to See Current Pricing for all Kinsta Hosting While Kinsta’s prices may seem high at first glance, keep in mind that they offer premium managed WordPress hosting that is designed for critical website applications that require more than what a general shared hosting plan provides. You should also consider that Kinsta includes many premium features that you would have to pay extra for with other WordPress hosts. See the Features section below for more details. Kinsta Features Choose From 27 Different Data Centers Data Centers in US, CAN, EUR, Asia, Australia, South America High Performance Cloud Infrastructure 24/7/365 Expert Customer Support Free Kinsta CDN with 275 Locations Edge Caching for Reduced Load Times Advanced Hosting Security Auto Wildcard SSL DDoS Protection Server-Level Full Page Caching Custom Designed Dashboard Analytics Reports Automatic Daily Backups Website Staging Application Performance Monitoring Free Hack Fixes DevKinsta for Free Local WordPress Development Free Site Migrations Kinsta API 30 Day Money Back Guarantee I am very impressed with the features that Kinsta includes with their hosting plans—quite possibly the best overall collection of features for a premium WordPress hosting plan. All of the features you would expect and need from premium managed WordPress hosting are there—and more. It starts with being able to choose your data center locations—and we’re not just talking about 2 or 3 choices here! Kinsta has data centers around the world in 27 different locations. So, whether you’re in the U.S., Canada, Europe, Asia, Australia, or South America, you can choose a server location that is closer to your own location. Having your website on a server closer to your area can help speed up your site. And, while we’re on the subject of website speed, Kinsta is powered by Google Cloud Platform and includes their Kinsta CDN to help speed up your websites even more. Currently, Kinsta’s CDN has 275 locations. See the Website Speed and Performance section below for more details. Edge Caching Edge Caching is definitely one of Kinsta’s best features. Kinsta’s Edge Caching technology allows your website content to be served from multiple data centers—greatly reducing your page load times and speeding up your website performance. Edge Caching reduces your sites TTFB (Time to First Byte) and complete page transfer times by an average of 50% or more. What’s also great about Kinsta’s Edge Caching is that it’s super easy to implement, and it eliminates the need to install plugins for caching and performance. DevKinsta Another Kinsta feature that deserves mentioning is their DevKinsta local WordPress development environment that is free to use. WordPress developers will really appreciate the ability to easily create sites and test changes out in a safe environment. DevKinsta includes an SMTP server for testing out email messages, and a built-in database manager tool. Kinsta Signup and Website Propagation So, let’s get started with our Kinsta test results.
